companion_apps.name: SAM Root
companion_apps.notes: Current successor app identified in the research store. A replacement BLE client needs neither this app nor a vendor account.

identity.notes: The local name is display data only because it can be changed by the robot's owner. The Device Information serial number is per-unit data; do not publish it in research notes or examples.

manufacturer_data.description: RT0: manufacturer payload after the two company-ID bytes starts with ASCII "RT0" (52 54 30). Require the Root Identifier Service as well; do not accept the service alone as proof of RT0.

methods.notes: Root RT0 candidate. The published protocol does not say whether any bytes follow the three-byte robot type, hence a prefix rather than an exact whole-payload match.

manufacturer_data.description: RT1: manufacturer payload after the two company-ID bytes starts with ASCII "RT1" (52 54 31). Require the Root Identifier Service as well; do not accept the service alone as proof of RT1.

methods.notes: Root RT1 candidate. Ci3 and every other robot-type string are out of scope until separately established for this protocol revision.

distributors.name: SAM Labs
distributors.notes: Current steward of the successor app and the successor-hosted official protocol repository. This does not assert that new RT0/RT1 hardware is still being manufactured.

manufacturer_data.description: Manufacturer-specific advertising data uses company ID 0x0600 (wire bytes 00 06). The payload begins with the ASCII robot type RT0 or RT1 for this spec. Ci3 is documented by upstream but deliberately excluded.

identification.notes: Require the Root Identifier Service and an RT0/RT1 manufacturer type as a narrowing pair. The service is the preferred scan filter because the local name is owner-renamable, but the same service family also covers robots outside this spec. Nordic UART is not an identification signal.

device.name: Root coding robot (RT0 / RT1)
device.notes:
Phone/direct-computer BLE coding robot. No cloud account, bridge or Wi-Fi provisioning is needed for the surface documented here.
SCOPE: only advertisements whose manufacturer payload identifies RT0 or RT1, and Root BLE protocol versions 1.0 through 1.3. The source calls 1.3 the current Root version and 1.4 planned, at the pinned 2024 snapshot. Create 3 / Ci3, protocol 1.5, and commands introduced only after Root 1.3 are not covered. Do not treat the shared Root Identifier Service alone as proof that a robot is in scope; check the manufacturer robot type too.
This spec intentionally declares only Device Information reads, Robot State, main-board versions, advertising name, battery state and the stop-and-reset command. It declares no movement, actuator, rename, bootloader, firmware-upload or firmware-activation operation.

openness.notes: The protocol was published for third-party clients. This spec is a deliberately narrow restatement for Root RT0/RT1, not a reconstruction from vendor internals. The current app was used only as evidence of successor continuity, not as the source of packet claims.

upstream_docs.covers: GATT profile, advertisements, Root protocol versions, packet layout and the safe commands declared here.
upstream_docs.title: Root Robot Bluetooth Low Energy Protocol Documentation

upstream_docs.covers: CRC-8 polynomial, initial value, input processing and absence of reflection/final XOR.
upstream_docs.title: Official CRC-8 reference implementation

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No pairing-mode button sequence, PIN or confirmation is described by the official protocol or its bare-GATT reference client.

exclusivity.recovery: If another client is holding the robot, disconnect it or close its app, then reconnect and subscribe. No bond needs to be forgotten. A power-cycle may drop a stale connection, but it is not a documented factory reset and its effect on persistent settings is unestablished.

pairing.notes: The published connection flow uses ordinary GATT without bonding or an application authentication exchange. This is reported from public source, not tested against a previously owned robot.

unpair.notes: Nothing to unpair: no bond is created. Host-side disconnect ends the session; general device 0 command 6 can request an immediate disconnect but is not needed for rebinding and is not declared as a command here.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi passphrase, account token, pairing key or application-layer credential is used by this spec. An owner-chosen advertising name is configuration, not an authentication secret.

factory_reset.description: Do not present stop-and-reset, disconnecting BLE, or power-cycling as a factory reset. A new client does not need a reset because no bond or owner credential is documented. The physical reset procedure, if any, remains an open research question.
factory_reset.effect: No owner-facing factory reset or list of cleared persistent state is established. Stop-and-reset (device 0, command 3) cancels pending actions and resets position; it is not proven to restore factory settings or clear the advertising name.

ble.protocol: Root BLE protocol 1.0–1.3 over Nordic UART

methods.description: No account or credentials. Use the Root Identifier Service to find candidates, accept only RT0/RT1 manufacturer types, connect, and subscribe before writing. Start with main-board versions to confirm that the unit speaks Root protocol 1.0–1.3.
methods.name: Direct BLE: identify, connect, subscribe

steps.action: Power on the Root robot and keep it stationary for the initial read-only checks.
Scan for the Root Identifier Service and accept only an RT0 or RT1 manufacturer robot type.
steps.expect: Root Identifier Service plus manufacturer payload beginning RT0 or RT1; no Ci3 match.

request.action: Scan and inspect manufacturer data for company ID 0x0600

steps.action: Connect and discover GATT services without starting OS pairing.
steps.expect: Root Identifier, Device Information and Nordic UART services are present.

steps.action: Subscribe to robot TX and wait for the subscription to complete before any write.
steps.expect: Notifications and/or indications are enabled on robot TX.

steps.action: Request main-board versions and check the returned BLE protocol version.
steps.expect: A matching response reports protocol 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3. Do not infer support for a newer version.

setup.notes: Nothing is provisioned. Power on, discover an RT0/RT1, connect without bonding, subscribe to the robot's TX characteristic, then issue safe queries. Medium confidence means this is the published flow, not one replayed by this project.

rejoin.notes: BLE-only: there is no Wi-Fi network or stored bond to rejoin. After the previous central disconnects, scan for RT0/RT1, connect and subscribe again. Whether two centrals can connect simultaneously is unknown.

steps.action: Disconnect the previous BLE central, including closing any app that is holding the connection.
Scan for the Root Identifier Service and the same RT0/RT1 manufacturer type, then connect.
Subscribe to robot TX before issuing another request; no factory reset is needed.

testing.notes: No RT0/RT1 hardware, advertisement dump, GATT dump, packet capture or on-device replay was used by this project. All protocol facts are reported from the official successor-hosted protocol repository at 8bac987096e984cb472843f8180fef142171df70. The packet vectors are constructed from those published rules, not captured from a robot.

variants.notes: Identified by manufacturer robot type ASCII RT0. Upstream says the color-sensor logical device is absent on RT0; no color-sensor command is declared here.
Identified by manufacturer robot type ASCII RT1.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Query replies and battery events share the same field offsets. Reject other logical devices and require a valid packet CRC before updating.

entities.name: Stop and reset activity
entities.notes: Cancels pending actions and stops the robot. It does not factory-reset the robot or clear its advertising name.

evidence.app_static_analysis: Research also checked the public SAM Root 3.1.0 app for successor continuity. No app-internal symbol, UI copy, firmware operation or new packet claim is imported into this spec. There was no hardware session or new capture.

artifacts.description: Source for discovery, GATT, Root protocol versions, framing, IDs and the four declared operations. Create 3 and motion/update behavior were reviewed only to exclude them.

artifacts.artifact: Root CRC reference and BLE example code at 8bac987096e984cb472843f8180fef142171df70
artifacts.description: CRC parameters and bare-GATT subscribe-first flow. No motor packet from the examples is copied or declared.
Successor continuity only. No hardware verification and no vendor-internal names or owner identifiers carried into this spec.

evidence.documentation_review: The official successor-hosted Root BLE protocol README, CRC implementation and example connection code at commit 8bac987096e984cb472843f8180fef142171df70 were read directly. The README is authoritative for UUID direction and packet semantics; the example's local UART variable labels are not used. The CRC's generated parameter block and bitwise update loop agree on poly 0x07, init/final XOR zero and no reflection.
evidence.open_questions: Current firmware/protocol support, physical reset behavior, Robot State flag masks, central exclusivity and write-without-response timing need an RT0/RT1 owner with hardware. A safe next experiment needs only an advertisement/GATT dump and version/name/battery exchanges.

initialization.notes: Robot TX must be subscribed before any request is written to robot RX. Enable every delivery mode the host supports and the characteristic exposes (notify and/or indicate), then wait for CCCD completion.

covers: Root/RT0/RT1 identification and Device Information reads
Main-board firmware, hardware, bootloader and BLE protocol version query
Advertising-name query and battery voltage/percentage state
not_covered: Movement, drive, actuator, rename and broader sensor commands are deliberately not declared
Firmware update, bootloader entry and firmware activation are deliberately not declared
Create 3 / Ci3 and protocol versions newer than Root 1.3
local_access.summary: Direct BLE from a phone or computer, with no cloud, account or bridge. Subscribe to robot TX before writing to robot RX.

packet_ids.events: Robot-initiated events use a separate unsigned 8-bit counter owned by the robot, also wrapping modulo 256. Never share a counter between host requests and robot events, and never assume an event with a numerically matching ID answers the current request.
packet_ids.requests: The host owns an unsigned 8-bit incremental counter, wrapping 255 to 0. An incremental ID of zero is always accepted and resets tracking; it is useful for stateless examples and recovery.
packet_ids.responses: A response copies the requesting packet's ID, so device, command and packet ID (bytes 0–2) all match the request.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Decode through the first NUL; a full 16-byte name need not contain one. Unused response bytes are zero.

scope.excluded: Create 3 / Ci3 and the separate Create 3 version table (including its 1.4/1.5 behavior); any Root protocol newer than 1.3 until separately proven. Upstream said 1.4 was planned, not released, at this snapshot.

test_vectors.provenance: Constructed from the published packet rules. Names and values are invented for documentation; no frame identifies or was captured from a real unit. payload_hex contains only significant bytes; the encoder left-justifies them and zero-fills the rest of the 16-byte payload.

remaining_unknowns: No owner advertisement/GATT dump or read-only packet exchange on current RT0/RT1 firmware exists here. All wire facts remain reported, and device.testing remains untested.

The pinned source is from 2024 and calls Root protocol 1.3 current and 1.4 planned. Whether current SAM-supported firmware changed the Root protocol is unknown; query versions rather than assuming continuity.
No factory-reset procedure, persistent-state clearing list or maximum simultaneous-central count is established. Stop-and-reset is not a factory reset.
The Robot State source diagram over-counts one bit while naming bump/touch/cliff flags, so this spec exposes only the low-seven-bit battery field and leaves individual flag masks undecoded.
Upstream does not specify whether manufacturer data contains bytes after the three-character robot type; discovery therefore uses an RT0/RT1 prefix, not a whole-payload equality claim.
Write-without-response requires host pacing but no interval is published. Use write with response until a safe interval is measured.

services.name: Root Identifier Service
services.notes: Empty by design: upstream specifies no characteristics. Advertise-filter on this vendor-specific UUID to find Root candidates, then apply the RT0/RT1 manufacturer-type restriction in device.identification.

characteristics.name: Serial Number
characteristics.notes: Upstream reports a 12-byte serial string. This is owner/unit identifying data: read it only when needed and never commit a real value to examples or research notes.

characteristics.name: Firmware Revision
characteristics.notes: Firmware version string, up to 12 bytes. This read-only GATT alternative does not replace the detailed main-board version query.

characteristics.name: Hardware Revision
characteristics.notes: Hardware version string, up to 12 bytes.

characteristics.name: Manufacturer Name
characteristics.notes: Manufacturer name string; upstream reports a 13-byte field. Do not infer the robot type from this string; use manufacturer advertising data.

format.name: state_flags
format.notes: Bump, touch and cliff flags. The pinned source's binary diagram has two leading zeroes plus seven flag labels, which cannot fit one byte; individual masks are therefore not asserted here.

format.name: battery_percent
format.notes: Low seven bits carry battery percent; bit 7 is outside the documented value.

characteristics.name: Robot State
characteristics.notes: Two-byte value also carried in advertising, allowing a scanner to distinguish a robot being touched before connecting. Read exactly two bytes. The advertising structure's outer encoding is not specified by the pinned source and is not guessed here.

get_battery_level.description: Battery logical device 14, command 1: query uptime, battery voltage and percentage. The matching response and unsolicited battery events share protocol_details.root_ble.response_layouts.battery_level but have command bytes 1 and 0 respectively.

crc.description: CRC-8 poly 0x07, init/final XOR 0, no reflection, over packet bytes 0–18.

packet_id.description: Host-owned request counter, modulo 256. Zero is always accepted and resets sequence tracking.

get_main_board_versions.description: General device 0, command 0: read main-board firmware, hardware, bootloader and BLE protocol versions. Board selector 0xA5 is main board. The response uses the same device/command/ID triple and is decoded with protocol_details.root_ble.response_layouts.get_versions_response.

crc.description: CRC-8 poly 0x07, init/final XOR 0, no reflection, over packet bytes 0–18.

packet_id.description: Host-owned request counter, modulo 256. Zero is always accepted and resets sequence tracking.

get_name.description: General device 0, command 2: read the current BLE advertising name. The response echoes device/command/ID and carries a UTF-8, NUL-terminated name in the 16-byte payload. This is a query, not the persistent rename operation (which is deliberately omitted).

crc.description: CRC-8 poly 0x07, init/final XOR 0, no reflection, over packet bytes 0–18.

packet_id.description: Host-owned request counter, modulo 256. Zero is always accepted and resets sequence tracking.

stop_and_reset.description: General device 0, command 3: immediately stop the robot, cancel pending actions and reset its estimated position. This is a safety/recovery action, NOT a factory reset. No response packet is documented. Movement commands that would make this necessary are outside this spec.

crc.description: CRC-8 poly 0x07, init/final XOR 0, no reflection, over packet bytes 0–18.

packet_id.description: Host-owned request counter, modulo 256. Zero is always accepted and resets sequence tracking.

characteristics.name: Robot RX (host writes)
characteristics.notes: Accepts exactly one 20-byte Root packet per write. Prefer write with response. Write without response is also documented, but then the host must pace packets itself; upstream gives no safe numeric pacing interval. Every template below includes its packet ID and final CRC.

format.name: timestamp_ms
format.notes: Milliseconds since the robot powered on.

format_match.notes: Decode the fields below only for logical device 14. Command 1 is a query response; command 0 is an unsolicited event. Other logical devices use protocol_details.root_ble.response_layouts instead.

characteristics.name: Robot TX (host subscribes)
characteristics.notes: Sends exactly one 20-byte packet per notification/indication. Validate length and CRC before decoding. A response repeats the request's first three bytes; an unsolicited event uses the robot's own independent event counter, so never correlate solely on packet ID. Subscribe before the first write to robot RX.

services.name: Nordic UART Service
services.notes: Standard Nordic UART transport carrying Root's fixed-size binary packets. RX/TX names are from the ROBOT's perspective, not the host's. This generic service is never sufficient for discovery by itself.
